To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

epidermal growth receptor (EGFR), ErbB- 2, and vascular-endothelial-growth-factor-receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) are expressed in human biliary tract carcinoma (BTC), and that EGFR and ErbB2 inhibition exerts marked in vitro and in-vivo effects, with NVP-AEE 788 being the most efficient drug.

epidermal growth factors and their receptors, as well as their downstream signalling molecules, are frequently expressed in biliary tract cancers, and that the inhibition of epidermal-growth-factor receptor signalling by the dual epider-mal-growth-factor receptor and Erb-B2 tyrosine-kinase inhibitor NVP-AEES88 is more efficient than inhibition by epidermal growth-factor-receptor antagonists in vitro, and in vivo in a chimerized mouse model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapeutic strategies against biliary tract cancer and other tumors with an aberrant epidermal growth receptor expression.
the development of novel therapeutic approaches for biliary tract cancer.
the molecular mechanisms of biliary tract carcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dual EGFR/HER2 inhibitor NVP AEES88 is a promising new drug for the therapy of biliary tract cancers.
epidermal growth-factor-receptor inhibitors are promising for the treatment of patients with biliary-tract cancer.
the dual EGFR and ErbB2 inhibitor NVP AEE788 was superior to the EGFR inhibitors gefitinib or erlotinib in vitro and in the chimeric animal model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dual EGFR and ErbB2 tyrosine-kinase inhibitor NVP-AEES788 is more efficient in inhibiting the growth of biliary tract carcinoma cell lines than the EGFR inhibitors gefitinib or erlotinib.
NVP-AEE787 is a promising new drug for the future treatment of biliary cancer.
NVP-AEE 788 is a potent inhibitor of biliary tract carcinoma cell proliferation, which is more efficient than gefitinib and more potent than erlotinib in vitro and in-vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NVP-AEE-788 is a potent anti-cancer drug in biliary tract cancers.
the dual EGFR/HER2 tyrosine inhibitor NVP-AEES88 is more efficient than EGFR tyrosine inhibitors gefitinib or erlotinib in vitro and in an in vivo chimeric mouse xenograft model.

the novel dual epidermal-growth-factor-receptor/ErbB- 2 tyrosine-kinase inhibitor NVP-AE788 has a more efficient effect than the epidermoid growth factor-receptor inhibitors erlotinib or gefitinib on biliary tract cancer cells.
